entities.summary:
Gil de Albornoz y Espinosa, called Egidio Carillo Albornozio in Italian sources, was a Spanish Catholic Cardinal who led the Spanish delegation at the papal conclave of 1644.

As a key figure in the Catholic Church during the Thirty Years' War, Gil de Albornoz y Espinosa played a crucial role in the political and religious landscape of Southern Europe.

His leadership during the conclave marked a significant moment in the history of the Church, as it highlighted the complex web of alliances and rivalries between European powers.

Despite his importance, Gil de Albornoz y Espinosa's life and legacy have largely been overshadowed by more prominent historical figures of the time.

The cardinal's dedication to his faith and his role in shaping the Church's response to the war make him a fascinating figure in the study of 17th-century European history.
